chunks: And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus.

Regarding a mute man who wrote on the ground the divorce of his wife, he said: If he does that at the beginning of the period of purity, with witnesses, and is understood from him as is understood from one like him, and he intends the divorce, then his divorce is valid according to the Sunnah.

key_terms.قُبُلِ الطُّهْرِ: Beginning of the period of purity

ai.seo_question: How does a mute man legally divorce his wife according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that a mute man’s written divorce is valid provided it occurs during the *qubul al-tuhr* (the period after menstruation ends but before intercourse) and is witnessed by those who comprehend his intent, aligning with the Sunnah. It underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on the clarity of intent (*niyyah*) and the role of witnesses in validating legal acts for those unable to speak, ensuring the divorce is not merely symbolic but legally binding.
